newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mixed amid crop jitters.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mixed amid crop jitters.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed mixed with the market recovering late on talk crop observers pegged the April 12-13 weekend freeze losses in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region at up to 290 million bushels, traders said.
"It kind of had a little pop when that came out but other than that there was not much going on," a trader said.

Oklahoma private consultant Dale Fain Tuesday said Oklahoma may struggle to produce 100 million bushels of hard red winter wheat this year, around half the total that might otherwise have been expected.
Fain said the crop potential in Kansas and Texas may also have been halved although he emphasized his information on those states was less extensive.
Flooding in the Northern U.S. spring wheat growing region and concerns about dry weather in portions of European wheat areas also underpinned the market.
Pressure came from signals the market was at technically overbought levels after the recent strong rallies.
MGE spring wheat futures closed 1-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with May up 1-1/4 at $4.65-1/4.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 30.350 million bushels, below the 36.704 million traded Monday.
MGE barley futures closed unchanged with May at $6.65 per cwt.
